accepted_knowledge.title: Diagnosing Payment Connector Pool Exhaustion
accepted_knowledge.text: Use this article when payment timeout rate rises together with payment connector active connections and downstream latency. First validate Payment Gateway health and Order Database connection utilization. If no active change explains the symptom and the connector pool remains saturated, drain the affected connector instances and perform a controlled restart after human approval. Do not restart the gateway or bypass approval.
accepted_knowledge.provenance: Governed free-text corpus with publication, validation, trust, and safety metadata

accepted_knowledge.title: Payment Timeouts Caused by Connector Exhaustion
accepted_knowledge.text: A prior incident showed database connection pressure beginning approximately fifteen minutes before payment timeouts. Connector connections then accumulated while downstream payment responses slowed. Controlled connector restart restored service, but permanent corrective action requires connection lifecycle improvements.
accepted_knowledge.provenance: Governed free-text corpus with publication, validation, trust, and safety metadata

accepted_knowledge.title: Digital Commerce Impact Evaluation
accepted_knowledge.text: Checkout failures and customer-facing HTTP errors represent high revenue and customer experience risk. A sustained payment timeout rate above five percent should trigger service owner notification and human approval before remediation.
accepted_knowledge.provenance: Governed free-text corpus with publication, validation, trust, and safety metadata

accepted_knowledge.title: Controlled Payment Connector Restart
accepted_knowledge.text: Prerequisites: confirm at least one healthy connector instance, validate Payment Gateway response time, check for active deployments, obtain approval, and drain traffic. Restart one instance at a time. Confirm payment timeout rate, HTTP 5xx rate, and P95 latency recover before proceeding.
accepted_knowledge.provenance: Governed free-text corpus with publication, validation, trust, and safety metadata

accepted_knowledge.title: Order Database Connection Saturation
accepted_knowledge.text: Investigate long-running transactions, pool churn, and application retry amplification. Database saturation can be a cause or a secondary effect. Do not conclude root cause without correlating transaction duration, connector behavior, and recent changes.
accepted_knowledge.provenance: Governed free-text corpus with publication, validation, trust, and safety metadata

conditional_knowledge.title: Payment Connector Timeouts May Indicate Gateway Protocol Incompatibility
conditional_knowledge.text: A gateway protocol negotiation incompatibility can produce payment timeouts and downstream latency that resemble connector pool exhaustion. Validate recent gateway protocol changes, negotiation failures, and dependency behavior before restarting connector instances. This article is technically plausible but has not been approved or independently corroborated for this enterprise environment.
